note: The rate base as a standing goal on a schedule: armed, then run now; the six steps run by themselves (the nine counted, the seven out) and the findings land.

journey.title: Quarterly rate base refresh: after every close
journey.prompt: After every quarterly close, refresh the Belmara rate base and update the schedules.

reads.res: Each quarter closes on the fourth working day; the next is the 6 November close for Q3, then 5 February 2027 for Q4
Six steps, one checkpoint, from the goal you just ran
Plant, depreciation and in-service dates, read fresh each run; the mailbox is read at run time
No regulatory list is connected; I need to know who to tell

questions.title: Who is told when it fires?
questions.text: No project-manager list is connected. The note goes out without waiting for you, so pick who should see it.

tiles.t: Me, the project managers and Procurement
tiles.s: Everyone who can change an order

nodes.title: State plant in service and depreciation by class
nodes.purpose: What Belmara has invested in plant, pipes and treatment, and what is left after depreciation.
nodes.how: Gross plant in service and accumulated depreciation by class at 30 September, from the fixed-asset ledger, at the approved depreciation rates; reconciled to the 2025 schedules.
nodes.check: Classes sum to the fixed-asset ledger; depreciation at the approved rates.

nodes.title: Test what is used and useful at 31 December
nodes.purpose: Which additions are in service at the test year end, and which are not.
nodes.how: The 38 post-test-year projects against the 12 October in-service file and the project managers’ replies; completed construction still in CWIP; the CWIP the order keeps out.
nodes.check: Every project is in, out or held, with the reason.

nodes.title: Roll the rate base forward from the 2025 order
nodes.purpose: From $776.9M at the 2024 test year end to 31 December 2026.
nodes.how: Additions and depreciation since the 2024 test year, the fourth-quarter additions and depreciation, then contributions, deferred taxes, advances, cash working capital and materials, in the RB-1 to RB-5 structure.
nodes.check: The roll-forward ties back to the $776.9M allowed and forward to the ledger.

nodes.title: Confirm how the nine completed projects in CWIP are treated
nodes.purpose: Stops here and asks you before the prudence review and the schedules.
nodes.how: Plant Accounting has not moved the nine yet. The schedules and the memo rest on how they are treated, and only you can confirm it.
nodes.check: Your answer is recorded on the plan before anything after it runs.

nodes.title: Check the prudence record of the major additions
nodes.purpose: Whether each addition above $2.5M can show it was prudently incurred.
nodes.how: For the twelve largest fourth-quarter additions: the WIN approval and its level, the business case, the award (bids, or a sole-source justification), and every change order with its approval.
nodes.check: Every addition has a complete record, or its gap is named.

nodes.title: What to present, and how
nodes.purpose: One rate base to present, with what it trades off.
nodes.how: Weigh presenting the seven out against keeping all 38 as filed, or holding for the close and the confirmations; state the trade-off and every caveat that reached it.
nodes.check: The recommendation names its remaining caveats and the alternatives it rejected.

nodes.title: Draft the schedules, the memo and the slides
nodes.how: Schedules RB-1 to RB-5 on the 2025 structure; a prudence and used-and-useful memo; a short deck for the 4 November session. Every figure linked to the step that produced it.
draws: Template: Belmara rate base schedules, 2025 case
nodes.check: Every figure links back to its step.

recs.title: Present $1,072.6M: the 31 on-track additions in, the seven dated 2027 out and listed for the next case
recs.summary: Schedules RB-1 to RB-5 at 31 December 2026 at the approved depreciation rates, with the nine completed projects counted as completed construction and the two prudence gaps closed before the 4 November session. The seven go on a separate list for the next case, each with the date it could come back in.
recs.tradeoff: About $4.4M a year of revenue waits for the next case, but nothing in the filing rests on a date the project managers have not confirmed.

story.text: Marc needs the Belmara rate base for DR-07 and DR-09 by 30 October.
Read plant in service and depreciation by class at 30 September.
Seven of the 38 post-test-year projects are dated 2027.
Read the order: plant counts only when in service at the test year end.
Nine completed projects are still in CWIP with certificates on file; they count.
Two of the twelve largest additions have prudence gaps.
Present $1,072.6M with the seven out, and close the two gaps before staff see the file.

recs.title: Present all 38 as filed, $1,113.9M, and update when the project managers confirm
recs.summary: Keep the seven in the schedules until the 6 November confirmations, then take out any still dated 2027 in the 13 November update.
recs.tradeoff: Keeps the revenue in the filing for now, but staff see a figure the order says will come down, and one project manager has already confirmed the slip.

story.text: Could the filing keep all 38 until the dates are confirmed?
Six of the seven dates are not yet confirmed.
The order removes anything not in service by 31 December.
Only worth it if the project managers correct their dates; otherwise the schedules come down on 13 November.

recs.title: Hold the schedules until the 6 November close and the confirmations
recs.summary: Wait for Plant Accounting to move the nine and for the project managers to answer, then file schedules where every figure is booked and confirmed.
recs.tradeoff: The cleanest record, but Marc goes into the 4 November session without schedules, and the update gets four days of review.

story.text: Could staff be given only booked, confirmed figures?
The close is 6 November; the confirmations are due the same day.
Marc needs the schedules on 30 October and meets staff on 4 November.
Only worth it if the session moves; otherwise present now with the open items named.

outputs.audience: Marc Beaulieu, for the BPUC record
outputs.purpose: Show the additions were prudent and are used and useful at 31 December 2026, with the two gaps and the seven taken out set out
outputs.template: Regulatory filings: prudence and used-and-useful memo

outputs.label: Belmara rate base: working session with BPUC staff
outputs.audience: BPUC staff, working session on Wednesday 4 November
outputs.purpose: Walk staff through the rate base, what changed since 2025, and what is held for the next case
outputs.why: Marc wants a few slides for the session on 4 November.

gaps: Six project managers have not confirmed their 2027 dates; answers are due 6 November, and a corrected date brings a project back in.
The nine completed projects move from CWIP to plant at the 6 November close; until then the ledger shows them in CWIP.
Two of the 31 on-track projects (CZZF5042_645, CZZF5025_640) have no row in the 12 October in-service file; their dates come from the post-test-year schedule.
